transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doc, I'm only sitting in this chair because everyone keeps harping on me, saying I’ve been doing too much. But frankly, it feels like I’m the only one left in the world with enough drive to actually get anything done. 

Take this move we're in the middle of—I'm the one who has to handle it and rebuild the new garage right. You can't trust contractors these days. I remember back when I was taking some drafting classes at the junior college, oh, must have been 1969 or '70, they taught us about proper load-bearing beams. You don't just throw up cheap pine and hope for the best. My brother-in-law tried that once on his shed and the whole roof sagged after the first heavy snow we got that winter. Cost him a fortune to fix. 

Anyway, so I'm handling the move, and I've got to organize things down at the church because the new committee couldn't plan a two-car parade if their lives depended on it. And on top of all that, I'm still at the plant, running the big industrial grinders. I swear I have to show these younger fellows at work how the job actually ought to be done every single shift. They just stare at their phones while the blending hoppers get all jammed up. I tell them, if you let a mixer seize up on my watch, you're gonna be chipping hardened aggregate out of there with a spoon. 

But yeah, I'm just making sure it all gets done right, and my family thinks it's some kind of problem.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, irritable, or energized lately, even when things aren’t going your way?

Well, I wouldn't say "unusually" energized, I'd say I finally have the energy to do what needs doing! But yeah, I guess I have been feeling like everybody needs to either get on board with my plans or just get the heck out of my way. I mean, I'll be feeling ten feet tall, making jokes, getting things sorted, and then my wife or my boy will ask some stupid little question and I just snap at them. 

Like yesterday, I was out in the driveway, measuring out the grade for the new concrete pour. You know, you have to get the slope exactly right or the water pools up against the foundation. My neighbor back in the 80s, Jim, he poured his own patio and didn't account for the runoff. First big storm we had, his basement flooded with three inches of muddy water. Ruined his wife's antique sewing machine. It was a Singer, one of those heavy cast-iron ones with the gold filigree. Beautiful machine. My mother had one just like it, used to make all my shirts when I was a kid. She could turn a collar so crisp you could cut your finger on it. 

Anyway, I'm out there working, feeling great, and my son comes out and asks if I want a sandwich. A sandwich! I'm in the middle of complex calculations, and he's interrupting me about cold cuts! I just went off on him. Told him if he wasn't going to hold the tape measure, he needed to go back inside and leave the real work to the men. He looked at me like I'd slapped him, but honestly, people just don't respect focus anymore.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep lately, or that you feel rested even if you haven't slept much?

Well, I haven't really been paying attention to the clock, to be honest. But I guess I don't need as much sleep as I used to. I mean, who has time for it? There's so much to do! I'll be up at 2 AM, wide awake, and I'll think, 'Why waste this time?' So I'll go down to the basement and start sorting through those old boxes of my dad's tools. 

He had this incredible collection of vintage Stanley planes. Beautiful craftsmanship. You don't see that kind of quality anymore. Everything now is just cheap plastic and stamped metal. It breaks after a year and you have to throw it away. Just like that toaster my wife bought last month. Two weeks in, the lever snaps off. I told her, 'I could fix that if I had the right spring,' but she just went and bought another one. Wasteful, I tell you. 

Anyway, where was I? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, I'll be up all night working on the tools or drawing up plans for the garage, and then I'll head into my shift at the plant feeling like a million bucks. No coffee needed! The guys at work think I'm crazy, but I just tell them they're soft. Back in my day, we didn't need eight hours of beauty sleep to get the job done. We just put our heads down and worked. Like my Uncle Ray. He worked two jobs, raised six kids, and still had time to build a boat in his backyard. A real beauty, too. Mahogany hull, brass fittings... he took us out on the lake in it a few times. Caught a bass so big once, it nearly snapped my line. Those were the days...
Have you found yourself talking more than usual, or feeling like your thoughts are racing so fast that others have trouble keeping up with you?

Well, I don't know about my thoughts racing, but I'll tell you what, once I start explaining what needs doing, the words just keep coming. It's like a faucet you can't turn off. My wife and my boy, they complain that I talk over them so fast they can't even get a word in edgewise to tell me to stop. But they just don't get the big picture! 

I have to explain it all, from A to Z. Like when I was telling them about the electrical wiring for the new garage. You can't just run a single 15-amp circuit and call it a day, not if you're going to be running heavy machinery. I remember this one guy at the plant, Tommy, he tried to wire his own workshop back in '98. Used 14-gauge wire for a 20-amp breaker. Can you believe it? Naturally, the wires got hot, melted the insulation, and nearly burned his whole house down. The fire department had to come out, and they used so much water his living room looked like a swimming pool. Ruined his wife's Persian rug. Real shame, too, it was an authentic one, brought over by her grandfather after the war. 

Anyway, so I'm trying to explain the importance of a dedicated subpanel, and they're just staring at me like I'm speaking Greek. I have to talk fast just to get all the information out before they lose interest and wander off to look at their phones again!
Have you been taking on more tasks than usual, or found yourself getting distracted easily while trying to focus on a specific job?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm taking on *more* tasks, I'm just finally getting around to the ones that have been piling up! But... yeah, I guess keeping my mind on one thing is getting tricky. Like, at the shop or at home, I'll be right in the middle of something important, and then—clank! One truck passes by, or I see one tool out of place, and boom, I'm off doing something else. Pretty soon I've got five things started and none of them finished. 

Like yesterday, I was polishing this huge brass fitting at the plant. Beautiful piece of metal, really. Reminded me of the brass rails on that boat my Uncle Ray built, the one I was telling you about. You know, brass is a funny metal. You have to use the right compound or it just streaks. I used to use this stuff called Brasso back in the day, came in a little tin can. You'd rub it on with an old rag—we used to use my dad's old undershirts, the cotton was so soft from being washed a hundred times. They don't make cotton like that anymore, it's all polyester blends now. Makes you sweat just looking at it. 

Anyway, I'm polishing this fitting, and I hear the forklift back up—beep, beep, beep. And I think, 'Hey, I need to check the tire pressure on my truck.' So I put the buffer down, walk out to the lot, and on the way, I see a stray bolt on the floor. Can't have that, someone could trip! So I pick it up, take it to the sorting bins, and realize the bins are a mess. So I start reorganizing the half-inch washers... and three hours later, the foreman is asking me why the brass fitting isn't done! I tell him, 'I'm improving the workflow!' but these guys, they just have zero vision.
Have you been making big plans or decisions lately that others might consider risky or out of character, like spending a lot of money, taking on major projects, or making sudden life changes?

Well, risky is a strong word, but I suppose I did make a few executive decisions lately. I went ahead and put some deposits down for the garage work and bought some new heavy equipment. I didn't exactly talk it over with my wife first, which... well, you know how that goes. She got that exact same look on her face she had back in 1985 when I bought our Airstream camper. Man, that camper was a beauty. Aluminum body, rounded edges, towed like a dream. We took it all the way out to Yellowstone that summer. You ever been out West? The geysers there are incredible. It is just pure thermodynamic pressure building up under the earth until it has to blow. Nature is the ultimate engine, if you really think about it. 

Anyway, where was I going with that... oh, the garage. Right, so I have just been driving back and forth between the houses trying to get everything set up. Racking up the miles on my truck. It has a 302 V8 engine, and let me tell you, they do not build them like that anymore. Now everything is computerized and you cannot even change a spark plug without a degree in computer science. I miss the days when a man could tune his own carburetor on a Sunday afternoon. 

So I am driving back and forth constantly, and then I am squeezing in my shifts at the plant, rushing through my grinding and polishing jobs so I can get back to my projects. A few of the guys at work, and the foreman too, they started warning me that I was taking chances, moving too fast around the machinery. But they just do not understand efficiency! They are all obsessed with safety regulations nowadays. Back when I started in the seventies, we did not have half these plastic safety guards getting in the way, and we got the job done twice as fast. You just have to respect the machine, that is all it takes...
Have you had any period in the last few weeks where you felt your mood was especially high, irritable, or energized for most of the day, nearly every day, even when things weren’t going your way?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm feeling "high," but I tell you what, I've been feeling like ten feet tall lately! Like I can tackle anything. But then, it's like... everybody else is just moving in slow motion, you know? And it gets under my skin. I feel like everybody needs to either get on board with my plans or just get out of my way! 

I'll be in a great mood, joking around, feeling fantastic, and then my wife or my boy will ask some little question—like, 'Why are there three new circular saws in the kitchen?'—and I just snap at them. I mean, it's obvious, isn't it? The kitchen island is the only surface flat enough to calibrate the blades! 

Speaking of blades, you really have to be careful with carbide tips. A lot of guys think you can just run them through any old material, but if you hit a hidden nail in a piece of reclaimed wood, it'll chip the carbide right off. Then you've got a projectile flying across the room at a hundred miles an hour. Happened to a buddy of mine, Frank, back in '82. He was building a deck out of some old barn wood. Beautiful wood, really, had that weathered gray look that people pay top dollar for now. They call it "rustic chic" or something on those home improvement shows. My wife watches those shows all the time. I tell her, 'Why are you watching a guy on TV build a bookshelf when you've got a master craftsman right here in the living room?' 

But anyway, yeah, I go from feeling great to just... snapping. Because they just don't see what I'm trying to do!

Have you had a period lasting at least a week where you felt unusually energetic or elevated most of the day, nearly every day, along with doing more goal-directed things—like starting new projects, making big plans, or pushing to get things done—more than you usually would?

Well, that is exactly why I’m here, honestly. Everyone keeps telling me I’ve been doing too much, pushing too hard for the last couple of weeks. But to me? It just feels like I’m the only one around with enough drive to actually get anything done! 

I mean, somebody has to get this move handled, and I have to make sure the new garage is rebuilt right because you just can't trust these modern contractors. And on top of that, I stepped up to organize things over at the church. 

Speaking of the church, they have this incredible old pipe organ in the sanctuary. Have you ever looked into the mechanics of a pipe organ? It is an absolute masterpiece of pneumatic engineering. Hundreds of wooden valves and leather bellows, all relying on perfectly balanced air pressure. It actually reminds me of the pneumatic presses we used to run at the old stamping plant back in '78. We had this one press, a real monster of a machine, took three guys just to calibrate the dies. One of the guys, old Sal, he actually lost half his pinky to that machine because he wasn't paying attention to the pressure release valve. Sal was a great guy, though. He made the absolute best smoked sausage you've ever had. He used this custom smoker that he welded himself out of an old fifty-gallon oil drum. You have to cure the metal first, of course, or the paint fumes get into the meat... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the projects. Yeah, so I'm handling the move, the garage, the church, and I still have to go in and show the younger fellows at work how the job actually ought to be done! Because if I don't push the pace, everybody else just sits around waiting for instructions.

But anyway, yeah, I go from feeling great to just... snapping. Because they just don't see what I'm trying to do!

patient.answer:
Well, that is exactly why I’m here, honestly. Everyone keeps telling me I’ve been doing too much, pushing too hard for the last couple of weeks. But to me? It just feels like I’m the only one around with enough drive to actually get anything done! 

I mean, somebody has to get this move handled, and I have to make sure the new garage is rebuilt right because you just can't trust these modern contractors. And on top of that, I stepped up to organize things over at the church. 

Speaking of the church, they have this incredible old pipe organ in the sanctuary. Have you ever looked into the mechanics of a pipe organ? It is an absolute masterpiece of pneumatic engineering. Hundreds of wooden valves and leather bellows, all relying on perfectly balanced air pressure. It actually reminds me of the pneumatic presses we used to run at the old stamping plant back in '78. We had this one press, a real monster of a machine, took three guys just to calibrate the dies. One of the guys, old Sal, he actually lost half his pinky to that machine because he wasn't paying attention to the pressure release valve. Sal was a great guy, though. He made the absolute best smoked sausage you've ever had. He used this custom smoker that he welded himself out of an old fifty-gallon oil drum. You have to cure the metal first, of course, or the paint fumes get into the meat... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the projects. Yeah, so I'm handling the move, the garage, the church, and I still have to go in and show the younger fellows at work how the job actually ought to be done! Because if I don't push the pace, everybody else just sits around waiting for instructions.
